question: Should OpenClaw core adopt this gateway-local multi-user identity and authorization model, including the public `api.teams` contract, as the permanent trust boundary for shared Workspaces?
rationale: The branch creates durable credential, session, device-pairing, delegation, storage, protocol, and external plugin API contracts; tests cannot determine whether these are the security and product boundaries maintainers intend to support.

options.title: Approve staged core design
options.body: Approve the threat model and API direction, then require staged, upgrade-proven changes before enabling the Teams portal.

options.title: Narrow to extension seams
options.body: Keep core changes limited to generic authorization and plugin hooks, with local accounts, sharing policy, and portal ownership outside core where feasible.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Do not adopt a multi-user gateway trust model until a maintainer-sponsored design is available.

recommendation.title: Approve staged core design
recommendation.body: Approve the threat model and API direction, then require staged, upgrade-proven changes before enabling the Teams portal.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Workspaces foundation and its core/plugin boundary were merged through this owner’s work, making them the strongest available decision-routing candidate.
